subject.title: fix(update): fail closed on managed plugin pin conflicts

question: Should this PR keep the install-layer conflict guard limited to the selected install root plus legacy project root, or must it also protect newer pins stored in other active generation roots?
rationale: The contributor’s follow-up and the retained-generation rollback test show that scanning every generation root is not a safe mechanical extension; deciding whether generation-root pins are user overrides or OpenClaw-managed rollback state requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Keep two-root scope
options.body: Treat other active generation roots as OpenClaw-managed rollback state for this PR, land the current fail-closed guard, and track any broader update-intent work separately.

options.title: Thread update intent now
options.body: Require this PR to add an update-layer signal that distinguishes bulk release-managed updates from explicit user downgrades before scanning active generations.

options.title: Pause for interactive UX
options.body: Hold the PR until interactive keep-pin/release-version/abort behavior and non-interactive flags are designed together.

recommendation.title: Keep two-root scope
recommendation.body: Treat other active generation roots as OpenClaw-managed rollback state for this PR, land the current fail-closed guard, and track any broader update-intent work separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He posted the current fail-closed policy direction and is already assigned to the PR.
